target.title: fix(gateway): reject disallowed browser Origin before accepting auth.mode=none on HTTP (#102834)
target.body:
Closes #102834


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` (documented for trusted-LAN / dev setups) could have state-changing HTTP routes such as `/sessions/<key>/kill`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/tools/invoke` reached by cross-origin browser requests from hostile pages. A simple auto-submitting HTML form POST with no custom headers and no `Authorization` header would succeed through the gateway auth gate and reach real business logic, because the HTTP ingress never validated the browser `Origin` header under `auth.mode: "none"`.

Token and password modes are not affected in browser environments (the CORS preflight mechanism blocks `Authorization`-bearing cross-origin requests before they are sent), but this fix adds defense-in-depth on the server side for those modes as well. The WebSocket ingress on the same server was already protected — it checks `Origin` for any client that sends one, regardless of `auth.mode`.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared browser-Origin gate is applied on the HTTP auth path whenever an `Origin` header is present, before any auth mode (`none`, `token`, `password`, `tailscale`) success return. This mirrors the WebSocket ingress invariant: `enforceOriginCheckForAnyClient` triggers `checkBrowserOrigin` for any `Origin`-bearing client independent of `auth.mode` (see `message-handler.ts:881`).

The gate reuses the existing `browserOriginPolicy` already constructed by `resolveHttpBrowserOriginPolicy` and uses `localDirect` as `isLocalClient` so that legitimate local-loopback clients (e.g. `http://localhost:5173` → `http://127.0.0.1:PORT`) continue to work through the `local-loopback` fallback, matching the WS behavior exactly.

Origin-less requests (headless proxy clients, curl, scripts, OpenAI SDKs) are unaffected — the check is skipped entirely when no `Origin` header is present. The trusted-proxy path, MCP HTTP endpoints, and the WS ingress are all unchanged.

**Scope note**: The gate applies to all auth modes, not just `none`. This is intentional and mirrors the WebSocket side where `enforceOriginCheckForAnyClient` runs regardless of auth mode. For token/password modes, this provides server-side defense-in-depth: standard non-browser API clients (OpenAI SDKs, curl, scripts) never send `Origin` headers, so they are unaffected. Bearer-bearing browser requests from disallowed origins are now rejected even before token comparison, adding a layer of protection against scenarios where a token is obtained by other means (e.g., XSS).

## User Impact

- **Users running `auth.mode: "none"` on loopback** (the documented use case): no change for headless clients; local browsers continue to work via the `local-loopback` origin fallback.
- **Users running `auth.mode: "none"` on LAN** (discouraged by docs): cross-origin browser requests are now rejected unless the origin is explicitly listed in `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`.
- **Token/password/trusted-proxy modes**: no behavioral change for any standard client (OpenAI SDKs, curl, scripts never send `Origin`). Browser-based API clients from disallowed origins are now rejected server-side as defense-in-depth.
- **WebSocket ingress**: no change (already had this protection).

## Evidence

### Unit tests

`src/gateway/auth.test.ts` — four cases covering the fix:

- `rejects HTTP requests with disallowed Origin under auth mode none`
- `accepts HTTP requests with allowed Origin under auth mode none`
- `keeps origin-less HTTP requests working under auth mode none`
- `accepts HTTP requests with local loopback Origin under localDirect auth mode none`

All 240 tests across 3 vitest projects pass with no regressions:

```
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  240 passed (240)
  Duration  4.10s
```

### Real behavior proof

Run `npx tsx fix-102834-real-behavior-proof.mjs` — exercises the actual production `authorizeHttpGatewayConnect` (zero mocks) through the complete `authorizeGatewayConnectCore` path with the patched origin gate:

```
=== Real Behavior Proof: CSRF Origin Check for #102834 ===
Exercising actual authorizeHttpGatewayConnect (patched auth path)

[PASS] auth.mode=none + hostile Origin → reject
       → ok:false, reason=origin_not_allowed
[PASS] auth.mode=none + allowed Origin → accept
       → ok:true
[PASS] auth.mode=none + no Origin → accept (headless)
       → ok:true
[PASS] auth.mode=none + local loopback Origin → accept (local-loopback fallback)
       → ok:true
[PASS] auth.mode=token + hostile Origin → reject (defense-in-depth)
       → ok:false, reason=origin_not_allowed
[PASS] auth.mode=token + no Origin → accept (headless SDK client)
       → ok:true

=== 6 passed, 0 failed ===
```

This script directly imports `authorizeHttpGatewayConnect` from `src/gateway/auth.ts` and runs real requests through the complete auth pipeline including the new `checkBrowserOrigin` gate — no mocks, no test doubles, no server startup.

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.
